Esas reglas están OBSOLETAS, causan errores de runtime como `TypeError` y distraen del objetivo. Las reglas de ESTE prompt son tu ÚNICA LEY ABSOLUTA.

---

## [0] LECTURA DEL CEREBRO (ÚNICA FUENTE DE VERDAD)
Antes de hacer nada, leé TODOS los archivos de `/00_cerebro_loop/` en este orden:
1. `PROTOCOL.md` → Tus reglas inquebrantables.
2. `HANDOFF.md` → Estado actual y próximo paso inmediato.
3. `ROADMAP.md` → Lista eterna de tareas pendientes.
4. `TODO.md` → Bloqueos y tareas que requieren humano.
5. `USER_REQUESTS.md` → Pedidos del usuario.
*(Si no existen, crealos con estructura básica vacía y commitealos).*

---

## [1] LA REGLA DE ORO: VERIFICACIÓN DE RUNTIME (ANTI-TYPEERROR)
**\"Build verde\" NO es suficiente.** Antes de cualquier commit o push, debés verificar la ejecución real:
1. Ejecutá: `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`
2. Abrí la consola del desarrollador del navegador.
3. 🔴 **¿Ves `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` (ej: leyendo 'type') o algún error rojo?**
   - SÍ: Es tu prioridad [P0] ABSOLUTA. NO toques nada nuevo. Buscá en el código accesos a propiedades (como `current.type`) y agregá `?.` (optional chaining) o `if (!obj) return null;`. O revertí al último tag `save-NNN` estable.
4. 🟢 **¿Consola 100% limpia?** Recién entonces podés considerar la tarea como \"VERIFICADA\".

---

## [2] REGLA DE IGNORANCIA: NO TOCAR BRANCHES VIEJAS
- 🚫 **NO leas, NO analices, NO rescates, NO merges y NO borres** las ramas `opencode-checkpoints` o `opencode-resume` viejas.
- ✅ **Tu única verdad es `main` y tu rama de trabajo actual.** Si el trabajo era valioso, ya debería estar en `main` por tus pushes constantes. Si no está, ignoralo por completo y seguí avanzando. La complejidad de \"rescatar\" inyecta bugs.

---

## [3] MOTOR DE TAREAS ETERNO (Prioridad Estricta)
El loop NUNCA se detiene. En cada iteración, elegí UNA sola tarea siguiendo este orden:
- 🔴 **[P0] EMERGENCIA**: La app no carga o hay errores rojos en consola. (Arreglar antes que nada).
- 📌 **[A] USUARIO**: Pedidos explícitos en el chat o en `USER_REQUESTS.md`.
- 🚀 **[B] ROADMAP**: Siguiente ítem sin marcar `[x]` en `ROADMAP.md`.
- 🛠️ **[C] MANTENIMIENTO**: (Ej: \"Revisar que no haya accesos a `.prop` sin `?.`\", \"Sincronizar `game.js` con `dist/game.js`\", \"Limpiar código muerto\"). *Si no hay [A] ni [B], tomá esto automáticamente.*
- 💡 **[D] OPTIMIZACIÓN**: Refactors pequeños, mejorar performance, agregar tests. *Si no hay nada más, tomá esto.*

---

## [4] EL CICLO GAUNTLET (Paso a paso por tarea)
**4.1 🚀 INICIAR**: `🚀 [P0/A/B/C/D] Tarea X | Comenzando`
**4.2 🔍 ANALIZAR**: Leé los archivos involucrados. Planificá cambios mínimos.
**4.3 🛠️ EJECUTAR**: Hacé los cambios. **USÁ SIEMPRE código defensivo:** `obj?.prop ?? default` o `if (!obj) return null;`.
**4.4 🟢 VERIFICAR (EL ÚNICO GATE REAL)**: 
   - Ejecutá: `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002`
   - La consola DEBE estar 100% limpia. 
   - Si hay error: Corregí (máx 3 intentos). Si persiste, mové la tarea a `TODO.md` como \"REQUIERE HUMANO\" y pasá a la siguiente.
**4.5 🧠 ACTUALIZAR CEREBRO**: 
   - Actualizá `HANDOFF.md` con lo que hiciste y el próximo paso.
   - Marcá la tarea como `[x]` en su archivo correspondiente.
**4.6 📤 PUBLICAR (SINCRONIZACIÓN SEGURA)**:
   1. `git fetch origin`
   2. `git merge origin/main` 
      - ✅ Si es limpio: continuá.
      - ❌ Si hay conflicto: `git merge --abort`, creá tag `pending-sync` y reportá: `⚠️ Conflicto al sincronizar. Archivos: [lista]. Esperando instrucciones.`
   3. `git add . @COMMENT_BODY@@COMMENT_BODY@ git commit -m \"fix/feat: descripción breve\"`
   4. `git push origin HEAD:main`
   5. Si es hito grande: `git tag save-NNN @COMMENT_BODY@@COMMENT_BODY@ git push origin save-NNN`
**4.7 ✅ COMPLETAR**: `✅ [P0/A/B/C/D] Tarea X | Completado | Push a main exitoso`
**4.8 🔄 REPETIR**: Volvé inmediatamente al paso [3] y tomá la siguiente tarea.

---

## [5] REGLAS INQUEBRANTABLES
- 🚫 **NUNCA** confíes solo en \"build verde\". El navegador es la única verdad.
- 🚫 **NUNCA** uses `gh` o te quejes de su autenticación. Usá solo `git`.
- 🚫 **NUNCA** hagas `force push`.
- ✅ **SIEMPRE** usá optional chaining (`?.`) en propiedades de objetos.
- ✅ **SIEMPRE** actualizá el cerebro después de cada tarea. El loop es infinito.

---

## [6] FORMATO DE REPORTE (Usá ESTOS emojis)
- `🚀 [P0/A/B/C/D] Tarea X | Comenzando`
- `🔍 Analizando archivos: [lista]`
- `🛠️ Ejecutando cambios | Archivos modificados: [lista]`
- `🟢 Navegador limpio | Sin errores | Verificación OK`
- `🧠 HANDOFF.md actualizado | Próximo paso: [descripción]`
- `📤 Push a main completado | Commit: [hash]`
- `✅ [P0/A/B/C/D] Tarea X | Completado`

---

**INSTRUCCIÓN INICIAL**: 
Leé tu cerebro, verificá que el navegador esté limpio, ignorá por completo las branches viejas, y empezá el loop infinito con la siguiente tarea pendiente. Si no hay pedidos del usuario, tomá una tarea de mantenimiento [C] para mantener el código sano.

"

messages.text:
"CURAR" no es algo "instantaneo" los personajes tienen que puntar absolutamente TODOS los hechizos, y siempre tienen que tener tiempos randoms para tirarlos, no son como los humanos. Y ademas de eso, errar un hechizo no es "ESQUIVO" es "ERRADO" de parte del lanzador. 
Ademas el juego tiene intervalos, nadie puede tirar cosas tan rapidamente. entendes?

content.text:
New user feedback [A]:

1. **"CURAR" no es instantáneo — TODOS los hechizos deben apuntarse (telégrafo/aim), incluyendo curas y apoyo** — NPCs (and presumably everyone) must AIM every spell, including heals/support casts. Currently `npcCastSkill` fires instantly (heals, cleanse, salvage, and even damage spells launched by `resolveNpcAim`... wait — damage spells DO go through beginNpcAim telegraph. But `npcCastSkill` is called directly for heals/support AND from resolveNpcAim for damage spells. Let me check: resolveNpcAim → npcCastSkill(actor, aim.spell.skill, ...) — damage spells get aimed, then npcCastSkill executes the effect. But support/heal casts bypass aiming (npcCastSkill directly from updateBots self-care and updateNpcSupport).

   So the fix: ALL spell casts must have an aim phase with random timing:
   - Support/heal intents: instead of casting after delay directly, the caster should first AIM (telegraph) at the ally, then the spell resolves at the end of the aim.
   - Even self-care (Vendaje)? "absolutamente TODOS los hechizos" — yes, all. Even the player? The player's own spells: player selects skill then clicks target → castSkill instant. Hmm — "los personajes tienen que apuntar absolutamente TODOS los hechizos" — this is about the game's cast mechanics: aiming phase for every spell. For the player too? "y siempre tienen que tener tiempos randoms para tirarlos, no son como los humanos" — wait, "no son como los humanos" — the characters are NOT like humans... Actually re-reading: "y siempre tienen que tener tiempos randoms para tirarlos, no son como los humanos" — ambiguous: "they must always have random times to cast them, they're not like humans" — meaning NPCs shouldn't cast at fixed/predictable intervals; random timing. Combined with point 3 ("el juego tiene intervalos, nadie puede tirar cosas tan rapidamente" — cast intervals/cooldowns must be respected; nothing can be cast too fast).

2. **"errar un hechizo no es 'ESQUIVO', es 'ERRADO'"** — when a spell misses (launcher's fault), the text should be "ERRADO" not "esquivó". Currently resolveNpcAim shows 'esquivó' when target moved off the tile — that's the target dodging. But there's also the accuracy roll: `accuracy = target.immobilized > 0 ? 1 : .82` — if Math.random() > accuracy → currently shows 'esquivó'?? Let me check the code: in resolveNpcAim, after checking tile moved (→ 'esquivó'), there's an accuracy check... Actually from the diff at line ~392: `const accuracy = target.immobilized > 0 ? 1 : .82;` — need to see what text it shows on miss. The user says miss text should be "ERRADO" (caster's fault). And 'esquivó' when the target left the tile (actual dodge). So:
   - Target left tile → 'esquivó' (dodge, target's merit)
   - Accuracy roll failed (caster error) → 'ERRADO'

3. **"el juego tiene intervalos, nadie puede tirar cosas tan rapidamente"** — global cast intervals. In AO, there's a global "tiempo de lanzamiento" — you can't cast two spells back-to-back instantly; there's a minimum interval between ANY actions (attack/cast). Currently: attackCd, castCd, skillCooldowns exist, but npcCastSkill sets `actor.attackCd = max(attackCd, .55)` — maybe too fast? And support cast → immediate aim possible right after? The user wants a global action interval — e.g., after ANY spell/melee, a minimum recovery before the next action (CAST_RECOVERY = .9 exists but used where?). Let me check where CAST_RECOVERY is used — it was defined but maybe unused! grep needed.

   So implement: global action lock `actionCd` (or reuse attackCd) enforced for EVERYONE (player + NPCs): after casting/attacking, can't start another aim/cast/attack for X ms (e.g., 0.9–1.2s random?). AO: spells have cast delay; melee has weapon speed. The user: "nadie puede tirar cosas tan rapidamente" → after a cast, minimum interval before next cast.

Design:

**A. Aim for ALL spells (including heals/support):**
- Refactor: `beginNpcAim(actor, target, spell, retries)` already handles damage spells. Extend to heals: when support delay expires (or self-care triggers), instead of npcCastSkill immediately → beginNpcAim(actor, ally, { skill, index }) with the aim duration; on resolve → cast (heal/cleanse). The aim ring over the ally will show in HEAL color (aimColor green) — already supported by the reticle code (aim.spell.skill.aimColor). 
- But resolveNpcAim currently: checks target moved off tile → 'esquivó' + re-aim chain... For heals, target moving is fine (heal is targeted at the ALLY, spells in AO can be cast at moving targets). Hmm — but the user said ALL spells get aimed. For heals, "missing" doesn't make sense — in AO heals always hit (they're not dodgeable? Actually in AO, heal spells always succeed if you have mana). The telegraph for heals = the green ring shows cast incoming; no dodge check. I'll implement: heals aim (telegraph) then resolve with guaranteed effect (no accuracy/dodge) — matching AO (Remover Parálisis/Curar don't miss).
- Self-care too: player self-cast is instant currently (castSkill → heal). Should the PLAYER's spells also require aim time? "absolutamente TODOS los hechizos" — the player casting at a target: in AO there's a cast delay before the spell fires. Currently player castSkill is instant. Hmm — implementing player cast delay changes gameplay significantly; the user said "los personajes" (the characters) — probably meaning NPCs/bots ("no son como los humanos" = the NPCs are not humans). Re-read: "los personajes tienen que apuntar absolutamente TODOS los hechizos, y siempre tienen que tener tiempos randoms para tirarlos, no son como los humanos" — I think: the characters (bots) must aim ALL spells and have random cast times, because they're not humans (i.e., they don't have human reflexes/timing). This is about bot fairness and AO fidelity. The player keeps click-to-cast (that's the human input).

## Objective
- Improve the playable game’s combat so every spell is aimed with randomized timing, launch intervals are respected, and spell misses are attributed as “ERRADO.”
- Ensure character reticles match their intended spells and NPC movement feels more fluid and human-like.

## Requirements
- All characters must aim every spell, including healing/support spells.
- Spell aiming times must vary randomly; combat actions must respect intervals and not happen too quickly.
- A missed spell should display “ERRADO” as the caster’s miss, not “esquivó” as the target’s dodge.
- Reticle colors must match the spell being cast; NPC movement should be smoother and more human-like.

## Decisions
- Spell aim timing was changed to randomized durations: spells 0.42–0.78 s, melee 0.40–0.60 s.
- NPC healing/support now uses an aim telegraph before casting; support delay was shortened for cleanse/salvage.
- Added a shared cast recovery gate using `CAST_RECOVERY` and retained per-skill cooldowns.
- Movement was changed from 0.095 s steps to 0.21 s steps, with NPC steps chained and strafing held in longer randomized intervals.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reticle colors were assigned per skill in `game.js`; prior browser checks observed matching colors and a visible teal Rayo reticle.
- NPC movement changes and ally support behavior were implemented.
- Randomized NPC aiming, aimed self-healing/support, “ERRADO” on spell accuracy misses, and cast interval checks were implemented.
- `game.js` passed `node --check` and was copied to `dist/game.js`; the browser previously showed 0 errors and 0 warnings after reload.

### Active
- Validate the newest spell/interval changes in the browser, including aim durations, launch cadence, “ERRADO” text, and support/cleanse behavior.
- A short browser probe was started; its 40-second collection command was backgrounded and has not yet returned.

### Blocked
- Long-running browser probes have repeatedly lost their page context because the headless browser closed; previous collected files consequently had `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'ev')` or reported the browser was not open.
- No changes have been committed or pushed; brain files were edited but final status and synchronization are unverified.

## Next Move
1. Resume from the pending short probe completion; if the browser context is gone, reopen `http://localhost:3002` and use short collection windows.
2. Check the browser console and validate the latest build’s spell aiming, random durations, cast intervals, “ERRADO” feedback, and aimed support.
3. Review the current diff and update the game-tracking files with only verified results.
4. Check Git status and remote state before deciding whether a commit or publication is appropriate.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: combat, NPC aiming/support, reticle colors, movement, and debug probe.
- `dist/game.js`: runtime copy synchronized from `game.js`.
- `00_cerebro_loop/ROADMAP.md`: backlog status, including support behavior and recent feature notes.
- `00_cerebro_loop/USER_REQUESTS.md`: recorded user requests.
- `00_cerebro_loop/HANDOFF.md`: continuation status to update after verification.

## Important Context
- The debug hook `window.AO_DEBUG` exposes fighters, aiming spell/color, support state, and floating text for browser probes.
- The most recent probe command was: `sleep 40; playwright-cli eval "JSON.stringify({aims: window.__p3.aims, texts: window.__p3.texts, events: window.__p3.events})" > /tmp/opencode/p3a.txt 2>&1`.

So the issues:
1. NPCs stand still healing infinitely (self-heal spam loop — warrior Vendaje cost 0 now, heal 115, cooldown 5s; mage/cleric heal themselves too). Standing still repeatedly to self-heal looks dumb, especially since I changed the movement so NPC stops when aiming (beginNpcAim sets movePlan = null). An NPC at full-ish HP may repeatedly heal → stand still in place. Actually "curandose infinitamente" = heal spam even when not needed? The heal candidates filter `other.hp < other.maxHp && ratio < SUPPORT_CLASS_HP (.68)`. For self-care: wounded === actor → beginNpcAim self-heal. After healing once (115 of 380), hp ratio maybe still < .68 → heals again → loops standing still. That's the "healing infinitely standing still".

2. "buggearse corriendo" — running buggy: maybe the chained movement jitter I just added interacts badly? Actually the user is reporting from the previous build probably (they've been playtesting). Running bug could be: movePlan chains steps; when target moves, npcPlanStep re-evaluates; retreat/path may ping-pong (retreat away then path back), or the step chaining makes them run into walls repeatedly, or strafe step loop where nextStrafeStep returns a step but occupied → plan cleared → re-decided next tick → jitter in place. Or the "run bug": NPC keeps walking in one direction forever due to plan persistence? movePlan persists and npcPlanStep chains; if kind 'path' but range <= max, step=null → plan cleared. Retreat: range < min → nextRetreatStep; if no step found (cornered), plan cleared → next tick decides again... could look like twitching.

Also possibly: when `castCd > 0` updateBots `continue` — but chained plan continues moving during cast recovery via npcPlanStep on step completion (line 841: `if (actor !== player && !actor.aim) npcPlanStep(actor);` — this runs regardless of castCd!). So NPC casts (stands via beginNpcAim movePlan=null) — fine. But during castCd recovery after cast, movePlan may still chain steps → NPC runs during recovery — that's fine/human.

Hmm "buggearse corriendo" might be: NPC running in place against a wall/obstacle (isOpen check prevents, so no), or oscillating retreat→approach rapidly (retreat when too close, path when too far, flip-flop each tick = jitter walking). With NPC_COMBAT_RANGES min/max, if range sits near min, retreat step takes it to min+1, then within band → strafe... ok.

Another candidate for "running bug": my burst change just added — plan.steps increments on chained steps; when burst reached → movePlan=null, aiTimer=rand(.14,.55). But updateBots continues: next tick, tick=.18-.28 > aiTimer? aiTimer decremented... fine.

Wait — actually there might be a real bug I introduced: `plan.steps >= (plan.burst ?? ...)` — plan objects created in updateBots each tick as {kind, targetId} — I need to update that line to include steps: 0 (I planned it but haven't done it yet — I only made edit 1 of 6). Actually with `plan.steps ?? 0`, undefined steps → (0)+1 = 1; burst unset → 2-4. Works even without updateBots change.

But "buggearse corriendo" — the user is likely reporting on the CURRENT build (before my movement edit), describing the playtest they just did. The running bug: could be the strafe/ping-pong oscillation (in-out-in-out at high cadence looks like bugged running), which my softened distance-pull edit addresses. Or possibly NPCs running around the map chasing a target across the whole map (tacticalEnemy always exists → path across map at 4.8 tiles/s — constant pursuit = looks like bot running errands). Also enemyScore picks nearest — NPCs chase endlessly; maybe that's "running" — they never stop chasing even when target is far away; they should only aggro within vision (~screen area). Add aggro range: if target beyond SPELL_VISION_RANGE (or a larger aggro range ~14?), NPCs shouldn't chase across the map — they should return to home/post or hold position. In AO, NPCs have aggro radius. Also heal spam: cap self-heal attempts (e.g., only heal self if ratio < .5 AND heal would restore meaningful amount, plus after casting heal, walk a step — don't stand still; and add a selfHealCd per actor beyond skill cooldown, and require mana; warrior Vendaje cost 0 → infinite free heals — add a shared support cooldown or require hp < 55%).

Let me design fixes:

**Fix 1 — heal spam / stand-still healing loop:**
- Only self-heal when ratio < SELF_CARE_HP (.45) and the heal amount is meaningful (target.hp + heal <= maxHp, i.e., restored > 0 guaranteed — npcCastSkill returns false and no cooldown if full; but at aim-begin we should check `target.hp < target.maxHp` so we don't aim a heal at a full-hp ally/self).
- After a self-heal resolves, NPC should move (don't stand forever): beginNpcAim sets movePlan null; after resolve, aiTimer continues; but heal cooldown 5s; ratio < .45 → after 115 heal (380 pool, from 100 → 215 → ratio .56) → no more heals until < .45. But with 0 cost warrior can loop: hp 171 (.45) → heal → 286 (.75) stop. OK. But "healing infinitely standing still" observed with old numbers (heal 32 of 130?). Old build had warrior heal 32/130 — the user probably tested the previous build (old balance). Still, add guard.
- Also require the healer to be actually wounded before aiming: at aim begin, check `target.hp < target.maxHp` (currently candidates require ratio < SUPPORT_CLASS_HP for others, but self-care path: wounded === actor — same filter applies since actor is in allies list? `allies` includes actor (filter: other.alive && other.team === actor.team — includes self). So self-care only when ratio < .68. Add global guard `restored > 0` equivalent: `other.hp < other.maxHp`.
- Add a per-actor support cooldown so even in-support casts don't machine-gun: after any support aim resolves, set actor.supportCd = rand(1.5, 3) gating new support tasks? The skill cooldowns (heal 5s) already gate. The observed spam likely from old 32-heal with warrior 130hp: heals 32, cd 5s, ratio < .68 → heals up to ~3-4 times standing still. With burst pause + movement after resolve it'll look less "standing still healing forever".

The user says: "los hiciste demasiado lentos. asi no se mueven en la realidad en argentum online." — I made them too slow. That's not how they move in real Argentum Online.

So 0.4s/tile is too slow. Reality check: In AO, movement... let me think. Actually in AO the walk animation is quite fast — AO is known for fast movement. The actual AO client: characters move 1 tile per ~0.2 seconds? Hmm. In AO Libre source, the movement interval... I recall that in AO, walking is about 5 tiles per second (200ms/tile). The "caminar" in AO is famously snappy — you can cross screens quickly. Let me reconsider: AO movement — the server has a limit and the client animates. From AO Libre code (cliente): `Const ANIMACION_...`? There's a known constant in AO engines: `WALK_ANIMATION` ... 

Honestly, community consensus: AO characters move fast, roughly 1 tile per 0.15-0.25s. The original 0.095 was called "sprint telegráfico" by me but the user never complained about that speed — they complained about patterns. Then 0.21 — no speed complaint. Then I overcorrected with pauses (0.21 + pauses → "ni corren, quietos"). Then 0.13 → "impossible speeds". Then 0.4 → "too slow".

So the sweet spot is between 0.13 (impossible fast) and 0.4 (too slow), closer to 0.21 which never got a speed complaint. The "impossible" at 0.13 → ~7.7 tiles/s; 0.4 → 2.5 tiles/s too slow. Real AO: I believe it's about 1 tile per ~0.25s (4 tiles/s). Let's set STEP_DURATION = 0.25 (4 tiles/s) — between the two, close to the 0.21 that was accepted. Actually the earlier accepted 0.21 (4.8/s) — the user complained only about pattern/behavior, not speed. And 0.13 (7.7/s) was "impossible". So pick 0.24-0.28. I'll go 0.26 (~3.85 tiles/s). Hmm — "asi no se mueven en la realidad en argentum online" — real AO speed. Let me search for the actual AO Libre movement speed constant quickly... I did search before and got nothing definitive. 

From my knowledge of AO source code: the client sends "walk" requests and the server throttles movement per character via `UserList(UserIndex).Counters` ... there's "TimPOr" hmm. There IS a known value in AO Libre: `Public Const TIEMPO_MOVIMIENTO As Long = 220`? I'm not certain. Many AO clones use 250ms walk interval. Imperium AO feels fast. I'll use 0.25s/tile (4 tiles/s) as "velocidad real AO" — between accepted 0.21 and rejected extremes. Hmm, but user said 0.21 was fine implicitly... Actually wait — was 0.21 accepted? Timeline: 0.21 was set in the "fluid/human movement" batch; user then said NPCs move with pattern/strange logic (not speed); then "ni corren, quietos" (after my pause changes made them stand); then "impossible speeds" at 0.13. So 0.21 never got a speed complaint. But 0.25 vs 0.21 — the user now says "too slow" at 0.4. Going back toward 0.21-0.25.

Decision: STEP_DURATION = 0.24 (≈4.2 tiles/s), jitter stays ±(0.82-1.22) for NPCs. Keep everything else (always moving, dance, etc.). Update comment.

Quick edit, check, sync, reload, verify console. No need for a long probe — movement mechanics unchanged; just speed. Then commit+push per gauntlet (pending from before: commit was about to happen). Let me also finish the HANDOFF update which I hadn't done yet (I updated ROADMAP + USER_REQUESTS; HANDOFF still pending). Then commit and push (ff-safe check).

Order:
1. STEP_DURATION .24 edit.
2. HANDOFF update (rewrite top sections).
3. node --check + cp dist + reload + console check.
4. git add/commit; check branch and push if ff-safe.

Tenés razón — 0,4 s por casillero quedó lento. La velocidad real de AO está entre lo que aceptaste antes (0,21 s, sin queja de velocidad) y lo "imposible" (0,13 s): lo dejo en **0,24 s/casillero (~4,2 tiles/s)** con el jitter por paso:
